claim: In Build's classic renderer a floor or ceiling tile is sampled as if each side were rounded DOWN to a power of two: a 64x400 tile on a floor shows only its first 64x256 and the rest is never drawn. Walls are not affected the same way.
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/tiles.cpp:281-292 tileUpdatePicSiz stores log2 rounded down; the floor rasteriser masks texture lookups with it: engine.cpp:2886 (setup_globals_cf1, sethlinesizes from picsiz, used by ceilscan and florscan) and :2951-2959 (ceilscan's masked and translucent cases)
use: Put only power-of-two tiles on floors and ceilings; rules_blood 'flat-tile-power-of-two' checks a map.

checked.how: Read NBlood/source/build/src/tiles.cpp:281-292 (tileUpdatePicSiz): j counts down from 15 while pow2long[j] > tilesiz, so picsiz holds log2 rounded down (400 -> 8, i.e. 256). engine.cpp:2802-2886 (setup_globals_cf1, called by ceilscan :2902 and florscan): :2886 sethlinesizes(picsiz&15, picsiz>>4) for the opaque floor; :2951/:2955/:2959 msethlineshift/tsethlineshift for masked and translucent floors. bloodmap/rules_blood.py:49 _flat_tiles_are_power_of_two, rule 'flat-tile-power-of-two' at :71.
